intent: Put AgentShield in CI so agent configuration is scanned on pull requests and critical findings fail the build.
summary: Added .github/workflows/agentshield.yml, the repo's first GitHub Actions workflow. It runs on pull_request only when the diff touches agent configuration (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, .hermes.md, .claude/**, .mcp.json, .husky/**) plus the workflow file itself, so a change to the gate re-scans, and it also exposes workflow_dispatch for manual runs. The job checks out, sets up Node 20, runs the exact command the acceptance criterion names, `npx --yes ecc-agentshield scan --path .` with --format json --output, then a second step reads summary.critical from the JSON and exits 1 if it is greater than zero, annotating the PR with ::error. I chose the JSON summary gate over the CLI's --gate flag after testing both: --gate exits 0 on this repository even with 13 high findings, because it compares against a baseline or score drop rather than failing outright, so it does not implement 'critical findings fail the build'. Verified locally that the tool runs, that the report has summary.critical = 0 on the current tree (121 findings: 0 critical, 13 high, 71 medium, 37 low), and that the exact gate command prints 0 and passes. Important honest limitation: I could not execute the workflow, since there is no GitHub Actions runner here and the repo had no .github directory before this card, so the YAML is validated by parsing, not by a green CI run. That is why the card is review and not done.

changes.note: First workflow in the repo: AgentShield on PRs touching agent config, JSON summary.critical > 0 fails the build, plus workflow_dispatch
PSI-097 claimed backlog -> doing -> review, owner agent:hermes

decisions.decision: Gate on summary.critical from the JSON report instead of the CLI --gate flag
decisions.reason: The acceptance criterion says critical findings fail the build. Tested --gate on this repo: it exits 0 despite 13 high findings, so it does not implement that rule. Reading summary.critical and exiting 1 on any critical is the literal behaviour the card asks for.
alternatives: Use --gate (rejected: does not fail on existing high/critical findings, only on new ones or score drops)
Use --min-severity critical (rejected: filters what is reported, does not set the exit code)

decisions.decision: Trigger on pull_request paths plus the workflow file itself
decisions.reason: The card names the agent-config paths; including '.github/workflows/**' means an edit to the gate is itself re-validated, and workflow_dispatch allows a manual run without a PR.

verification.manual: Ran the real scanner locally: `npx --yes ecc-agentshield scan --path .` works and produces 121 findings (0 critical, 13 high), so the gate passes on the current tree. Ran the exact gate command (`node -e ... summary.critical`) against the JSON report and it printed 0. Parsed the workflow YAML with PyYAML to confirm structure, triggers, path filters and steps. The workflow itself was NOT executed - no GitHub Actions runner is available in this environment and the repo had no .github before this card - so this is unproven in CI until the first PR that touches these paths runs it.

risks: The workflow has never run on a GitHub runner. The npx install of ecc-agentshield needs network access on the runner, and the node require() of the JSON report path assumes the scanner wrote it; the gate step checks for the file and fails loudly if it is missing.

0 critical findings today means the gate is green on the current tree; its real value only shows when a future change introduces a critical finding, which cannot be demonstrated until such a change exists.

follow_ups.note: Confirm on the first PR that touches an agent-config path (or a workflow_dispatch run) that the job is green, then a human stamps review -> done (C-21).
The scan reports 13 high and 71 medium findings, mostly MCP template/example inventory rather than live config. A separate task could triage them; out of scope here (C-02).

human_review.reason: The workflow cannot be executed without a GitHub runner, so CI enforcement is unproven until the first PR or a manual dispatch run. Also 13 high findings exist in the scan; the gate only fails on critical, by design per the acceptance criterion.
